summary: Midday reserved-capacity wobble caused by validator-sweeper ephemeral reservations and soft-reserve contention
description:
Issue summary:
During the midday traffic window on 2026-03-10, LuminaSearch observed a 30–60% reduction in steady-state throughput for their reserved dedicated pool in us-east. P50 latency increased modestly but p99 and token throughput showed periodic collapse for short bursts (~2–7 minutes). Impact: customer-facing search features experienced slowdowns and occasional 5xx fallbacks.

Impact:
- Affected customer: LuminaSearch (dedicated)
- Window: ~2026-03-10 12:10–13:05 UTC with recurring micro-wobble through the afternoon
- User-visible: search ranking queries retarded; fallback model invocations triggered

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) – prod-us-east
- Model: redwood/gpt-medium-v2 pinned by customer
- Autoscaler config: target_utilization=0.75, cooldown=120s, min_replicas=2, max_replicas=10

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Customer traffic reproduces normal bursty search pattern (many short single-token prompts, many concurrent connections).
2) At roughly 12:10 UTC, internal validator-sweeper jobs started a background sweep that spawns ephemeral validation requests against pinned models for telemetry.
3) Within 60–90s of sweep start, autoscaler trimmed new allocations and observed slot scarcity; throughput collapsed transiently and customer routes fell back to slower variants.

Observed metrics / logs:
- scheduler.allocation_miss rate spiked by 4x at 12:11 UTC
- autoscaler.decisions shows repeated shrink events followed by rapid grow (thrash) between 12:11–12:18 UTC
- GPU_slot_utilization per-node dropped 10–40% while pending_queue_length rose
- Validator-sweeper emitted many short-lived connections with keepalive=false (seen in sidecar logs)
- Sidecar metrics flagged many ephemeral attachments with small compute duration (<200ms)

Additional notes:
- No driver crashes or node reboots during window
- No direct network partition; control-plane health green
investigation_notes: 12:15 - Support: alerted by LuminaSearch CS about repeated p99 spikes and fallback to smaller model variants.
12:20 - Observability: found correlation between validator-sweeper runbook schedule and start of throughput wobble (internal cron at 12:10 UTC).
12:28 - SRE hypothesis: ephemeral validator jobs create many short attachments that soft-reserve allocator credits and compress heartbeat signals, confusing autoscaler sampling windows.
12:35 - Instrumentation: captured sidecar logs showing 8k ephemeral attach/detach events in a 6-minute span, avg lifetime 180ms; many from internal service validator-sweeper@infra.

12:48 - Confirmed: autoscaler sampling window uses decayed moving averages that underweight short-lived attachments, leading to repeated shrink decisions during the sweep. Shrink then starves longer-lived customer streams that get queued, causing throughput drop and grow oscillation.
13:00 - Experiment: disabled validator-sweeper in us-east staging. Immediate reduction in attach/detach churn and stabilization of autoscaler decisions in 2 mins.

13:20 - Found related config: validator-sweeper had recently been updated to increase concurrency from 5->40 without registering with resource-controller; change merged in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/582.

13:35 - Root-cause working theory: combined effect of (a) high-frequency ephemeral validator attachments that consume allocator credit in short bursts, and (b) autoscaler cooldown and sampling heuristics that misinterpret short-lived spikes as capacity release, causing under-provisioning for steady customer load.
13:50 - Cross-team sync: SRE, Serving, and Platform scheduled a mitigation and longer-term fix planning session.
comments: Support (Amelia): Logged customer impact and opened incident. Notified on-call SRE.

SRE (Devon): Looking at autoscaler logs; seeing shrink/grow oscillation coincident with high attach churn. Investigating whether allocator credit accounting treats ephemeral attaches as 'free' and then releases too quickly.
Customer (LuminaSearch-SA): Observed search latency issues beginning 12:10 UTC; provided sample request IDs and traces (trace 8b3f7d). Asking for ETA on mitigation.
Platform (Marta): Disabled validator-sweeper schedule in us-east at 12:30 UTC as a test. Noted immediate improvement. Will roll back change if additional impact seen.
SRE (Devon): Temporary mitigation applied — throttled validator-sweeper concurrency and enabled attach debouncing in allocator config. Monitoring for 30 minutes.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation: throttled internal validator-sweeper concurrency in prod-us-east, and applied attach-debounce (10s) in allocator to prevent credit thrash from sub-second attaches. This stopped the autoscaler oscillation and restored steady throughput for LuminaSearch by 12:35 UTC.

Permanent plan: (1) change validator-sweeper to use non-reserved telemetry path (no GPU attaches) or run sweeps on dedicated validation capacity; (2) update autoscaler sampling to weight longer-lived streams more heavily and add a short attach-debounce window before allowing shrink decisions; (3) add a safety circuit to prevent shrink if pending_queue_length > threshold. Owners: infra-team (sweeper changes) and autoscaler-team (sampling/decisions). Target ETA for permanent fixes: 2026-03-24.

Follow-ups: postmortem and config changes tracked in Confluence (see related page). Customer compensation request: LuminaSearch CS to engage commercial team if credit remediation is requested.
